key_insight: An empirically calibrated differential game models driver interactions more accurately than tested baselines while producing verified approximate equilibria.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports realistic intersection simulation without hand-written priority rules, with safety and comfort parameters adjustable to engineering targets.
method: Model drivers with delayed perception and costs for speed, lane adherence, control effort, gap keeping, conflict, and contact.
Solve the general-sum differential game using feedback iterative linear-quadratic optimization.
Calibrate ten behavioral parameters per vehicle through Bayesian optimization of observed trajectories.
evidence_signal: Using data from four Washington, D.C., intersections, calibration achieved 1.00 m mean position error for 819 vehicles; route-only prediction achieved 7.42 m on 96 held-out vehicles, with ten-fold cross-validation showing significant gains over tested baselines.
watch_item: Untuned safety parameters led to collisions in 43% of tight closed-loop conflicts; safety-targeted weights and a stiffer contact barrier eliminated collisions in those tests, not necessarily in broader deployment.
paper_title: Empirically Calibrated Differential Games for Simulating Driver Interactions
